groups.label: Adeimantus's Challenge
groups.summary: Adeimantus criticizes the conventional praise of justice based merely on external rewards and reputation. He demands that Socrates prove the inherent value of justice and the harm of injustice within the soul alone.
groups.rationale: Both items represent Adeimantus's unified Book II challenge demanding an intrinsic defense of justice.

groups.label: Civic and Cultural Purging
groups.summary: Socrates establishes regulations over poetry, lies, musical modes, instruments, and judicial qualification. These measures aim to banish lamentation, luxury, and moral corruption to properly mold the character of the city's protectors.
groups.rationale: Coherent sequence of Book III passages establishing civic purges across storytelling, music, and the judiciary.

groups.label: Guardianship and Civic Myth
groups.summary: Socrates details the selection and rigorous testing of the elder rulers, distinguishing them from their younger auxiliary supporters. He introduces the civic myth of the metals to anchor social roles and hereditary placement.
groups.rationale: Focuses on the recruitment, trial, stratification, and foundational myth for the ruling class in Book III.

groups.label: Communal Institutions and War
groups.summary: After Adeimantus demands clarity on communal living, Socrates outlines collective family arrangements and mating controls for the guardians. He further specifies codes of warfare that restrain violence and enslavement among Hellenic peoples.
groups.rationale: Encompasses the Book V proposals regarding communal domestic institutions and pan-Hellenic military conduct.

groups.label: Philosophers' Nature and Status
groups.summary: Socrates defines true philosophers by their love for all wisdom and the direct apprehension of truth rather than superficial appearances. Adeimantus counters that actual lifelong practitioners of philosophy are commonly seen as useless or corrupt.
groups.rationale: Captures the Book V–VI debate defining the nature of the philosopher in contrast to popular skepticism regarding their social utility.
